summary.oneLiner: A small-cap Pune-based civil-infrastructure EPC contractor that inflected hard in FY26 — revenue +42% to Rs 243 cr, Q4 revenue +174% YoY to Rs 109 cr, PAT +65%+ to Rs 25.7 cr — riding a record Rs ~1,854 cr order book (~2x book-to-bill; ~Rs 2,000 cr+ after post-year-end wins). The pitch is a **Class 1A unlimited licence** (bids large government tenders solo, no JV margin-sharing) plus niche higher-margin verticals (Metro-BMS, tunnel ventilation, sports pools via Myrtha, data-centre cooling) where competition is lower. Management guides to Rs 600 cr (FY27) / Rs 900 cr (FY28) revenue with ~17–18% EBITDA and 10–11% PAT margins — a steep >2x scale-up that is largely execution- (not order-win-) dependent given Rs ~1,500 cr of backlog executable by FY28.

one-line thesis: A small-cap Pune-based civil-infrastructure EPC contractor that inflected hard in FY26 — revenue +42% to Rs 243 cr, Q4 revenue +174% YoY to Rs 109 cr, PAT +65%+ to Rs 25.7 cr — riding a record Rs ~1,854 cr order book (~2x book-to-bill; ~Rs 2,000 cr+ after post-year-end wins). The pitch is a Class 1A unlimited licence (bids large government tenders solo, no JV margin-sharing) plus niche higher-margin verticals (Metro-BMS, tunnel ventilation, sports pools via Myrtha, data-centre cooling) where competition is lower. Management guides to Rs 600 cr (FY27) / Rs 900 cr (FY28) revenue with ~17–18% EBITDA and 10–11% PAT margins — a steep >2x scale-up that is largely execution- (not order-win-) dependent given Rs ~1,500 cr of backlog executable by FY28.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Adjustments/flags: (a) FY-EBITDA rupee figure ("14.61 cr") contradicts the 17.10% margin — verify against filed results. (b) Q4 revenue +94.88% QoQ is POC-driven (percentage-of-completion) — mgmt confirmed no profit is booked below 25% project completion, so new-site mobilization mechanically depresses near-term margin. (c) Share capital "tripled ~Rs 1,199 → 3,598" (figures in lakhs) via bonus + preferential — dilution already taken.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue: FY27 ~Rs 600 cr; FY28 ~Rs 900 cr; framed as ">2x revenue CAGR in the current year." ~Rs 1,500 cr of the existing order book is slated for execution by FY28.

New order target (FY27): minimum Rs 1,000 cr of new orders/pipeline this financial year. Not bidding in Q1; will bid from end of Q2. Explicitly no revenue inflow modelled from the new pipeline this FY (design-build lag — revenue starts only after design/build phase). New wins would be additive to the 600/900 cr guide.
Margins: PAT margin held at 10–11%; EBITDA 17–18% "easily" for FY27 and FY28. All contracts carry price-escalation clauses, so raw-material/war-driven inflation is passed through.
Cash flow: operating cash flow turned positive in FY26; positive OCF expected again in FY27. D/E ~0.3 to stay "within limits."
Capex/new segments: tunnel ventilation first order ≥6 months out; data-centre (liquid-to-liquid cooling) order visibility deferred to the Q2 call; Aligarh JV long-dated (see §8).
order book & pipeline: Rs 1,854 cr closing order book (Mar-26), spread across 5 states (Maharashtra, UP, Gujarat, Haryana + one more) — deliberately de-concentrated by geography.

Q4 fresh orders Rs 1,317 cr — marquee Tier-1 clients: MMRDA (Metro Line 6) and L&T (Metro Line 4). Two major metro wins (associated with L&T and IRCON) referenced as large-ticket. Public-project payment milestones keep the WC cycle clean.
Post-year-end: new Rs 100 cr order from IRCON + an Aligarh order → order book ~Rs 2,000 cr+.
Sports-complex pipeline ~Rs 244 cr growth; positioned for 2030 Commonwealth/Olympic-linked sports-infra bids via Myrtha Pools.
Key growth segments per mgmt: Metro and sports.
segment / subsidiary detail: Metro (core growth): civil + in-house Metro-BMS; Pune Metro executed via T&T and ANSH JVs (hit qualification bars without locking 100% own capital).
Sports infrastructure: Myrtha Pools (Italy) tie-up — Olympic official partner; described as a near-"monopoly" edge for premium sports/pool bids; low own-overhead.
Net-zero / green buildings: via Bootes Infra LLP, expanding North-India footprint at 16–17% operating margins.
Niche verticals: Metro-BMS, tunnel ventilation, data-centre works — "lower competition → better margins than regular civil work."
In-house model: firefighting, all electrical, and works done in-house; purchases direct from OEMs — cited as the margin/rate advantage vs large EPC players who sub-contract.
Revenue recognition: percentage-of-completion, conservative — no profit margin recognized below 25% project completion (only cost = revenue until then, then full POC).
growth verticals / optionality: Data centres — liquid-to-liquid cooling: in process of tie-up with foreign tech companies; will inform shareholders before entering; no order-book commitment yet (update promised at Q2 call). Ties to the Data-Center theme.
Tunnel ventilation: new segment; doing R&D, onboarding consultants, seeking tie-ups; first order ≥6 months away.
Aligarh land-monetization JV (49%): real-estate/land-sale optionality — long-dated (see §8).
Sports/net-zero: "perfectly timed" for Olympic/Commonwealth bid cycle and green-building demand.
margins & cost dynamics: Raw-material / war-driven inflation flagged by analysts — mgmt says all contracts include escalation clauses, so inflation is passed through and "will not hurt margins."

Q4 EBITDA margin (13.94%) below the FY 17.10% level because multiple large new sites were mobilized simultaneously (front-loaded setup costs + conservative <25%-completion no-profit policy) — mgmt expects normalization.
In-house execution (electrical, firefighting, BMS) vs peers' sub-contracting is the cited margin lever; OEM-direct purchasing keeps bid rates competitive.
Finance cost down 6.59% (FY) despite balance-sheet growth — driven by equity/warrant inflow, not debt refinancing.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Aligarh land-monetization JV: Univastu share 49%; project timeline 96 months; pay government 90% after 96 months (i.e., after sale proceeds are received); total revenue ~Rs 250 cr at ~20% EBITDA; realisation spread over ~78–96 months — long-dated, back-ended.
Tunnel ventilation: first order min 6 months out; R&D + consultants + potential tie-ups underway.
Data-centre cooling: foreign-tech tie-up in progress; no capex/order numbers committed yet.

Funding of scale-up: cash-credit limits from Canara Bank + HDFC Bank; own funds; ~Rs 14 cr warrant inflow due July (MD personally subscribed to warrants "last week" to bridge the gap); warrant balance payable within 18 months (early tranche due July). Mgmt asserts this is sufficient and cash flow is "handled wisely"; D/E to stay ~0.3.
capital allocation: Warrants + preferential are the primary funding lever (also the reason finance cost fell); MD subscribing personally = skin-in-the-game (but adds dilution on top of the FY26 bonus + preferential that tripled share capital).
Working-capital discipline: matching payables cycle (~90 days) to receivables; ~85–87% of year-end receivables collected within ~30–45 days post year-end.
risks & watch-items: Steep scale-up execution: ~Rs 240 cr FY26 → Rs 600 cr (FY27) → Rs 900 cr (FY28) is a ~2.5x jump in two years; mgmt says teams, plant & machinery and major procurement are already in place ("ahead of time," "no risk currently") — credibility check pending.

Working-capital intensity / government receivables: trade receivables rose sharply (chat-box flagged a >10x jump — mgmt clarified the figure is in lakhs not crores, ~Rs 80–87 cr, ~80% collected within 30 days); classic government-EPC payment-cycle risk.
Funding dependence on warrants/preferential: if warrant subscription or milestone collections slip, the WC bridge tightens; further dilution possible.
Aligarh JV is very long-dated (78–96 months) — optionality, not near-term value.
Nascent verticals (data-centre cooling, tunnel ventilation) have no orders yet — narrative optionality until Q2 update.
Margin-mix risk as revenue scales via large metro contracts (typically lower-margin than niche work).
management quality / tone: Promotional, confident tone; several answers were vague or garbled ("easily possible," "H1 vs H2 will be great"), and the FY-EBITDA rupee figure looks misstated — precision on numbers is a watch-item.

Positives: MD personally subscribed to warrants (alignment); proactively clarified Jiya Eco is not a Univastu acquisition; explained the conservative <25%-completion revenue-recognition policy; addressed receivables lakhs-vs-crores confusion.
Declined to comment on share price ("dull movement" question) — appropriately.
non-obvious takeaways: Class 1A unlimited licence is the structural edge — lets Univastu bid large government tenders on its own merit without sharing margin with JV partners; underpins the solo-bid, in-house-execution margin story.

The 600/900 cr guide is more execution- than order-dependent — ~Rs 1,500 cr of the existing backlog is already slated for FY28, and mgmt models zero revenue from new FY27 wins, so new orders (target ≥Rs 1,000 cr) are pure upside.

Q4 margin dip is mechanical, not structural — the <25%-completion no-profit POC policy means a wave of new-site mobilization front-loads cost and defers profit; normalization is a policy artifact, verifiable next quarter.

Niche-vertical strategy (Metro-BMS, tunnel ventilation, Myrtha pools, DC cooling) is explicitly a margin-defence play against commoditized civil-EPC competition — but three of these are still pre-order.
Dilution is the quiet cost of the growth: FY26 bonus + preferential tripled share capital, and more warrants are being issued to fund the scale-up.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
